question: to the Commission Davor Ivo Stier (PPE), Karlo Ressler (PPE) Subject:

The Commission is negotiating an EU-INTERPOL cooperation agreement. Parliament’s 5 July 2022 recommendation requested purpose limitation, transfer limits, independent oversight and judicial redress. Parliament’s resolution of 16 June 20261 and the 8 July 2026 Hague resolution of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly2 warn that sanctioned states weaponise INTERPOL notices, together with asset freezes, against those states’ critics in exile. Comprehensive sanctions do not prevent a state from accessing INTERPOL and other interstate channels. The Assembly identified a Russian method to extract funding abroad for its war economy: structures acting for the state, reportedly including Alfa-Bank, combined INTERPOL notices and civil claims with asset freezes in order to bring about the takeover of Baltic Bank and the detention of Andrei Isaev in France in 2020 on an INTERPOL request, whose claims European courts executed even after Alfa-Bank was sanctioned in 2022. 1.
How will the Commission give binding effect to the 5 July 2022 safeguards, and will it require an additional review of requests from sanctioned states such as Russia, or their proxies?
Will it apply the source-based approach under Regulation (EU) 2024/31923 to refuse, by default, cooperation on the basis of requests from states systematically engaged in transnational repression?
Will it create an EU-level appeal mechanism against abusive notices, publish notice statistics by issuing state, and guarantee redress, including banking access?

Parliament resolution of 16 June 2026 on countering transnational repression – towards an EU strategy to protect Europe’s sovereignty and democratic values, texts adopted, P10_TA(2026)0203. 2 Hague resolution of 8 July 2026 on countering transnational financial repression and the weaponization of INTERPOL executive management, anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism, and cybersecurity. 3 Council Regulation (EU) 2024/3192 of 16 December 2024 amending Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia’s actions destabilising the situation in Ukraine,OJ L, 2024/3192, 16.12.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/3192/oj. 1
